title: Luciferase reporter assays to monitor interferon signaling modulation by SARS-CoV-2 proteins
protocol: Detach HEK293T cells with trypsin.
Count living cells using dye exclusion (Erythrosin B or Trypan blue Stain).
Adjust the concentration and volume of the trypsinized cells in DMEMxxx for the seeding.
Seed 4×10^4 cells in 48-well plates in 250 μL DMEMxxx per well to achieve 60–70% confluency the next day.
Discard the leftover of the seeding solution.
Incubate for 18 h at 37°C and 5% CO2 in a humid atmosphere.
Seed HEK293T cells such that confluency is between 60 - 70% after 18 hours.
Transfect the HEK293T cells using TransIT-LT1 18 h post seeding.
Prepare the mix of DNA constructs in 25 μL Opti-MEM for one 48-well according to Table 2.
Fill up each DNA-Opti-MEM mixture to the same amount of total DNA with empty vector.
Add TransIT-LT1 (3 μl per μg DNA) to the DNA-Opti-MEM mixture and mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the transfection mixture for 15 min at 20°C–25°C.
Carefully add the transfection mixture dropwise to the cells.
Replace the growth medium in the wells with 200 μl per well of DMEMxxx containing the respective IFN in the appropriate amount.
Replace the growth medium of the negative control (no stimulation) with 200 μl per well of DMEMxxx lacking the stimulant.
Incubate for 8–48 h, depending on the stimulant used.
Quantify luciferase activity for type I, II, and III interferon signaling using F-Luc reporters controlled by the respective promoters.
Measure cell viability based on ATP metabolization in the cell lysate using CellTiter-Glo.
Normalize measurements using R-Luc expression from the pGAPDH-R-Luc construct.
Normalize measurements using G-Luc expression from the pTAL-G-Luc plasmid.
Remove supernatant and add 100 μL 1× Passive Lysis Buffer per 48-well.
Shake gently for 15 min at 20°C–25°C until a fluffy white precipitate is formed.
Optional: Freeze and thaw the plate at −20°C to improve cell lysis and have a more uniform signal.
Transfer 25 μL of cell lysate into a type white 96-well plate.
Add one volume (25 μL) of the Dual-Glo Luciferase Reagent.
Shake cautiously and incubate for at least 10 min at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Measure the F-Luc signal with a Luminometer using standard settings, 0.1 s measurement time per well on an Orion II microplate Luminometer (Berthold).
Quantify the signal of your internal control (normalization) of choice.
Add one volume (25 μL) of Dual-Glo Stop & Glo Reagent to the plate from step 3.
Shake cautiously and incubate for at least 10 min at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Measure the R-Luc signal with a Luminometer using standard settings, 0.1 s measurement time per well on an Orion II microplate Luminometer (Berthold).
Transfer 25 μL of cell lysate into a type white 96-well plate.
Add one volume (25 μL) of CellTiter-Glo Reagent.
Shake cautiously and incubate for at least 10 min at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Measure luciferase signal using the Orion II microplate Luminometer within 30 min.
Prepare Coelenterazine solution as described in the buffers and media section of the materials and equipment chapter.
Store Coelenterazine solution as 100 μL aliquots at -80°C.
Thaw one aliquot (100 μL) of Coelenterazine solution and mix it with 20 mL 1× PBS.
Prime the luminometer by inserting an external priming container/plate into the luminometer.
Place the reagent injector cable in a tube with ultrapure water.
Place the reagent injector cable in a tube containing the previously prepared Gaussia substrate.
Prime the injectors with the Gaussia substrate as recommended by the manufacturer of your device.
Remove the external priming container/plate.
Transfer 25 μL of supernatant into a type white 96-well plate.
Agitate gently to evenly distribute the sample within the well.
Set volume of injected substrate to 50 μL per sample.
Record G-Luc activity over a period of 1 s per sample with a delay of 2 s following substrate addition.
Insert the plate and start the measurement.
Use cell lysates from step 13 to confirm proper expression of viral proteins by western blotting.
Transfer 30 μL of lysates to a tube and pellet cell debris at 20,000 g, 4°C for 20 minutes.
Quantify protein amount using a BCA assay according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Adjust samples to a concentration of 1 μg/μL using 1× Passive Lysis Buffer.
Transfer a volume equal to 10 μg of total protein to fresh tubes and add 6× SDS-PAGE Loading buffer to reach a final concentration of 1×.
Boil the lysates at 95°C for 10 minutes to denature proteins.
Load one lysate per pocket in a NuPAGE 4%–12% Bis-Tris Gel.
Load a pre-stained protein marker to estimate the size of viral proteins.
Run the gel at 90 V for 90 minutes in 1× MES-SDS running buffer.
Transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane using semi-dry western blotting.
Place the membrane in 1% casein in PBS to block free protein binding sites for 60 min at 20°C–25°C while gently agitating.
Incubate the membrane with an anti-strep II-tag antibody (diluted 1:2,000) in PBS-T with 0.05% Casein at 4°C for 16–24 h.
Wash the membrane three times for 5 min in PBS-T.
Incubate the membrane with an IRDye 680RD goat anti-rabbit IgG secondary antibody (diluted 1:20,000) in PBS-T with 0.05% Casein at 20°C–25°C for 30 min.
Wash the membrane three times for 5 min in PBS-T.
Quantify the fluorescence of the secondary antibody using a Li-Cor Odyssey Scanner.
Incubate the membrane with an anti-GAPDH antibody (diluted 1:1,000) in PBS-T with 0.05% Casein at 20°C–25°C for 1.5 h.
Wash the membrane three times for 5 min in PBS-T.
Incubate the membrane with a secondary antibody (IRDye 800CW goat anti-rat IgG secondary antibody, diluted 1 to 20,000 in PBS-T with 0.05% Casein) for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Quantify the fluorescence of the secondary antibody using a Li-Cor Odyssey Scanner.
